themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints spiked to 16 THIS WEEK—a 256% jump from the 4.5-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting a concentrated noise disturbance problem affecting multiple blocks in Flatbush/PLG this week.
evidence: 16 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (256% spike, z-score: 7.67)
Highest statistical severity among all current spikes; isolated to single week
No corresponding Reddit or news mentions yet—emerging story with limited public awareness
reporting_angles: Identify which streets/intersections are generating complaints; interview affected residents about sleep/quality-of-life impact
Investigate whether spike correlates with specific event (concert, street racing, construction) or enforcement gap

themes_detail.label: Drinking & Street Disorder Surge
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints jumped 300% THIS WEEK to 4 complaints from a 1.0-per-week baseline, and non-emergency police matters spiked 261% to 14 complaints this week vs. 3.9 weekly average—indicating a possible uptick in street-level disorder or homeless encampment activity this week.
evidence: Drinking complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (300% spike, z-score: 3.46)
Non-emergency police matters: 14 THIS WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average (261% spike, z-score: 5.52)
Repeating CB budget requests for homeless services expansion and street outreach suggest underlying structural problem
reporting_angles: Map the geographic concentration of these complaints; interview residents and local business owners about visible street disorder
Connect spike to known homeless service sites or encampments; assess whether DHS outreach capacity is adequate

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked 208% THIS WEEK to 5 complaints from a 1.6-per-week baseline—a unusual clustering that may signal sanitation or pest control failure, or reflect broader environmental health issue.
evidence: 5 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (208% spike, z-score: 4.85)
Concentrated in single week; no prior pattern evident in 90-day data
Aligns with elevated unsanitary condition complaints (704 over 90 days, second-highest category) but dead animals specifically rare until now
reporting_angles: Determine whether complaints cluster in specific neighborhoods or parks; interview DSNY about removal response times
Investigate whether spike correlates with rodent/pest activity or reflects seasonal pattern beginning

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Outbreak Concern
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints reached 3 exactly THREE WEEKS AGO, a 380% spike from the 0.6-per-week baseline—while no longer spiking this week, this recent cluster warrants investigation to rule out restaurant outbreak or food supply contamination.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average (380% spike, z-score: 3.41)
Spike has not recurred in subsequent weeks, suggesting either resolved incident or reporting lag
No corresponding news or Reddit mentions; potential unreported public health issue
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with DOHMH food inspection data for Flatbush/PLG; identify which establishments triggered complaints
Interview health department about whether complaint cluster triggered investigation or closure

themes_detail.label: Building Code/Use Violations Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints spiked 153% exactly THREE WEEKS AGO to 6 complaints from a 2.4-per-week baseline, occurring amid 354 active DOB permit filings—raising questions about construction management and code enforcement during active renovation wave.
evidence: 6 building/use complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.4 weekly average (153% spike, z-score: 3.26)
354 total DOB filings in past 90 days (204 alterations, 97 new buildings, 8 full demolitions) suggest high construction activity
Spike timing correlates with active permit period; could indicate enforcement or contractor compliance gaps
reporting_angles: Obtain details on which buildings generated complaints; assess whether violations involved safety, occupancy, or zoning
Interview DOB about complaint response times and whether inspector capacity is adequate for current permit volume
